questions.prompt: The wise fear nothing, but the foolish tremble at every shadow.
questions.answer: Sapientēs nihil timent, sed stultī ad omnem umbram tremunt.

questions.prompt: The Greeks conquered the Trojans by cunning rather than by strength.
questions.answer: Graecī Trōiānōs dolō potius quam vīribus vīcērunt.

questions.prompt: The brave often help the weak in war.
questions.answer: Fortēs saepe īnfirmōs in bellō adiuvant.

questions.prompt: Small things delight boys, but great things attract kings.
questions.answer: Parva puerōs dēlectant, magna autem rēgēs alliciunt.

questions.prompt: The gods know all things, both the true and the false.
questions.answer: Dī omnia sciunt, et vēra et falsa.

questions.prompt: Many desire great things, few endure hard things.
questions.answer: Multī magna cupiunt, paucī dūra patiuntur.

questions.prompt: Time reveals hidden things and overthrows the mighty.
questions.answer: Tempus occulta aperit et magnōs ēvertit.

questions.prompt: This wise man envies no one, although he owns little.
questions.answer: Hīc sapiēns nēminī invidet, quamquam parva possidet.

questions.prompt: A certain learned man wrote many books about the stars.
questions.answer: Doctus quīdam multōs librōs dē astrīs scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The honest man, content with little, harms nobody.
questions.answer: Probus, parvō contentus, nēminī nocet.

questions.prompt: A Roman man does not fear death for his country.
questions.answer: Vir Rōmānus mortem prō patriā nōn timet.

questions.prompt: The learned praise the ancients, the unlearned scorn them.
questions.answer: Doctī veterēs laudant, indoctī contemnunt.

questions.prompt: Our men fought bravely while the enemy were fleeing.
questions.answer: Nostrī fortiter pugnāvērunt dum hostēs fugiunt.

questions.prompt: The rich, forgetful of the gods, often neglect the poor.
questions.answer: Dīvitēs, deōrum immemorēs, pauperēs saepe neglegunt.

questions.prompt: The good obey the laws; the wicked scorn them.
questions.answer: Bonī lēgibus pārent, malī eās contemnunt.

questions.prompt: The wise poet compares great things with small ones in his song.
questions.answer: Sapiēns poēta magna parvīs in carmine compōnit.

questions.prompt: Nature has hidden many things from mortals.
questions.answer: Nātūra multa ā mortālibus occultāvit.

questions.prompt: New things delight the crowd, old things delight the learned.
questions.answer: Nova vulgus dēlectant, vetera doctōs.

questions.prompt: This brave man defended his country against many foes.
questions.answer: Hīc fortis patriam contrā multōs dēfendit.

questions.prompt: A certain foolish man believed the false rather than the true.
questions.answer: Stultus quīdam falsa potius quam vēra crēdidit.

questions.prompt: The learned man teaches useful things, the orator pleasant ones.
questions.answer: Vir doctus ūtilia docet, ōrātor iūcunda.

questions.prompt: The immortals grant good things to the pious.
questions.answer: Immortālēs bona piīs tribuunt.

questions.prompt: The powerful oppress the humble, but the gods defend the innocent.
questions.answer: Potentēs humilēs opprimunt, sed innocentēs deī dēfendunt.

questions.prompt: Few endure difficult things, but many flee the harsh.
questions.answer: Paucī difficilia tolerant, multī autem aspera fugiunt.

questions.prompt: This wise man, content with little, teaches the young many things.
questions.answer: Hic sapiēns, parvō contentus, iuvenēs multa docet.

questions.prompt: The honest envy no one, the wicked fear everyone.
questions.answer: Probī nēminī invident, improbī omnēs metuunt.

questions.prompt: A certain brave man saved the citizens from great dangers.
questions.answer: Fortis quīdam cīvēs ē magnīs perīculīs servāvit.

questions.prompt: We seek the true and flee the false in all matters.
questions.answer: Vēra petimus, falsa fugimus, in omnibus rēbus.

questions.prompt: Nothing new delights the old, nothing ancient the young.
questions.answer: Nihil novī senēs iuvat, nihil antīquī iuvenēs.

questions.prompt: The learned seek something true amid many errors.
questions.answer: Doctī aliquid vērī inter multōs errōrēs quaerunt.

questions.prompt: The pious hope for good things, the wicked fear evil ones.
questions.answer: Piī bona spērant, scelestī mala timent.

questions.prompt: That prudent man foresees future things and remembers past ones.
questions.answer: Ille prūdēns futūra prōvidet et praeterita meminit.

questions.prompt: In the midst of the battle the brave stood firm.
questions.answer: In mediō proeliī fortēs stetērunt.

questions.prompt: The powerful often scorn useful things and pursue empty ones.
questions.answer: Potentēs saepe ūtilia contemnunt et inānia sequuntur.

questions.prompt: The wise bear adverse things with a calm mind, the foolish yield to them.
questions.answer: Sapientēs adversa aequō animō ferunt, stultī iīs cēdunt.

questions.prompt: A certain rich man built temples and gave much to the poor.
questions.answer: Dīves quīdam templa aedificāvit et pauperibus multa dedit.

questions.prompt: Great things are accomplished by the diligent, small ones neglected by the idle.
questions.answer: Magna ā dīligentibus geruntur, parva ab ignāvīs negleguntur.

questions.prompt: The good praise honorable things, the wicked mock sacred ones.
questions.answer: Bonī honesta laudant, malī sacra dērīdent.

questions.prompt: The old remember many things, the young hope for greater ones.
questions.answer: Senēs multa meminērunt, iuvenēs maiōra spērant.

questions.prompt: This eloquent man persuaded the doubtful with true words.
questions.answer: Hic disertus dubiīs vērīs verbīs persuāsit.

questions.prompt: Fortune favors the bold and abandons the timid.
questions.answer: Fortūna audācēs iuvat et timidōs dēserit.

questions.prompt: Something certain is sought by all amid uncertain things.
questions.answer: Aliquid certī inter incerta ab omnibus quaeritur.

questions.prompt: The immortals see all things, both hidden and open.
questions.answer: Immortālēs omnia vident, et occulta et aperta.

questions.prompt: A certain cruel man oppressed the weak and feared the strong.
questions.answer: Crūdēlis quīdam īnfirmōs oppressit et validōs timuit.

questions.prompt: In the midst of dangers the faithful never desert their friends.
questions.answer: In mediō perīculōrum fidēlēs amīcōs numquam dēserunt.

questions.prompt: The prudent choose useful things, the reckless pursue harmful ones.
questions.answer: Prūdentēs ūtilia legunt, temerāriī noxia sequuntur.
